title: kbgit.py upstream brings the upstream main into the clone by its scope's policy and lists the local commits that change upstream-owned paths
goal: kbgit.py upstream fetches the upstream remote alone and brings its main in by the scope kbpublic.clone_scope reads (me rebases the clone's local commits onto it, team and org merge it into main without rewriting a commit the integration remote holds) as git.md writes the policy down; it lists each local commit that changes a path the upstream main also tracks, marking one whose change the upstream main now holds as resolved upstream with the revert to drop it; --dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing; the gate and the push stay kbgit.py sync --push

run: import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kbgit.py','upstream','--help'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and '--dry-run' in p.stdout else 1)

clauses.clause: kbgit.py upstream fetches the upstream remote alone and brings its main in by the scope kbpublic.clone_scope reads (me rebases the clone's local commits onto it, team and org merge it into main without rewriting a commit the integration remote holds) as git.md writes the policy down
it lists each local commit that changes a path the upstream main also tracks, marking one whose change the upstream main now holds as resolved upstream with the revert to drop it
--dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing
the gate and the push stay kbgit.py sync --push

notes: Premise (field report 2026-10-19): the Windows clone carries local edits of tracked upstream files (tests_ceiling.json win32 1800, its decision row) next to its own setup; no tool tells which local commits touch upstream-owned paths or which of them upstream now makes unneeded, so each fetch from GitHub would meet them as conflicts. The public main is a projection that fast-forwards on every publish (git.md, Public home), so a team clone seeded from it can take it by merge without rewriting its own pushed commits. Depends on ST-s6iz6z36 for kb.upstreamRemote. Operator's answer 2026-10-19 replaces the removed gate policy: the bring-in follows the scope table (me rebase, team and org merge; ST-s6iz6z36 notes). The test upstream_merge plants one clone per scope.
